To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the acetylcholine-evoked neuronal firing excitation is dependent on the rate of the spontaneous activity and that this effect is regulated by changing the membrane properties and expression of the cholinergic reaction, which may reflect the changing of K+ membrane permeabilty.

acetylcholine regulates the spontaneous activity of cortical neurons via the modulation of the dendritic properties and the cholinergic reaction of the neurons, and this effect is dependent on the rate of the spontaneous activity of the neurons.

acetylcholine evoked excitation in cortical neurons is depended on the rate and pattern of spontaneous firing, which in turn is regulated by the expression of the cholinergic reaction and dendritic properties.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of spontaneous activity in the regulation of cholinergic excitation.
the regulation of neuronal activity in somatosensory cortex under the effect of cholinergic system.
the regulation of spontaneous neuronal firing by the effect of acetycholine.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
acetylcholine regulates the rate of spontaneous firing by changing the K+ membrane permeabilty.
acetylcholine regulates neuronal firing in somatosensory cortex by changing K+ conductance and dendritic properties of cortical neurons.
cholinergic excitation in the cortex may have an effect on neuronal firing rate by means of regulation of K+ conductance.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
cholinergic system in the cortex is not only a modulator of synaptic transmission but also it is a modulator of the spontaneous neuronal activity.

acetylcholine is an important factor for the control of spontaneous firing rate of cortical neurons and it is a part of the mechanisms that are responsible for the regulation of the neuronal activity.
cholinergic excitation of cortical cells is not a result of a single mechanism but rather a complex process that involves several factors.
The main takeaway from our work is that
acetylcholine regulates the firing rate of cortical neurons in a complex and multifactor manner.
acetylcholine, acting through muscarinic receptors, is capable of regulating neuronal excitability in the cortex by affecting dendritic properties and cholinergic reactions.
acetylcholine is an important factor in regulating the excitability of cortical neurons in vivo.
